statement: No top-3 compute jurisdiction bans or licenses open-weight release at the frontier tier (official gazettes; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Holding (no ban or licence) at end-2025. A Bloc A export rule (Jan) put a licence requirement on closed model weights above 1e26 FLOP but expressly exempted published (open) weights; it was not enforced from May. Bloc A's July national AI plan actively encouraged open-weight models. A non-bloc regional union began obligations for general-purpose model providers (Aug), with partial open-source exemptions that do not cover systemic-risk models; these are transparency and safety duties, not a release licence. Bloc B policy in 2025 promoted open source; its existing service filing regime covers public-facing services, not weight release (not re-verified this run).

items.summary: A Bloc A interim final export rule created a licence requirement for weights of closed models trained with >=1e26 operations. It explicitly excluded published (open-weight) models and models weaker than the best open-weight model, stating no controls on open-weight models were being imposed.
items.detail: Bloc A BIS 'Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion', 90 FR 4544 (published 2025-01-15, effective 2025-01-13), new ECCN 4E091, Note 1.

items.summary: Two days before the compliance date, the Bloc A commerce agency told enforcement officials not to enforce the January rule and announced a rescission and future replacement, so even the closed-weight control lapsed in practice.
items.detail: Bloc A Department of Commerce press release, 2025-05-13 ('Rescission of Biden-Era AI Diffusion Rule'); the formal rescission was not completed within 2025.

items.summary: Bloc A's national AI action plan had a section 'Encourage Open-Source and Open-Weight AI'. It said release decisions are 'fundamentally up to the developer' and the government should create a supportive environment, which signals no near-term licensing.
items.detail: White House, 'Bloc A's AI Action Plan' (July 2025), Pillar I.

items.summary: A non-bloc regional union's general-purpose AI model obligations took effect. Open-source models get partial exemptions, but models with systemic risk (presumed at >1e25 FLOP) must still notify, evaluate and mitigate. These are post-release duties, not a ban or licence on release. Its position among the top-3 compute jurisdictions is uncertain (~3% of AI supercomputer performance by one count).
items.detail: Bloc C AI Act (Regulation (Bloc C) 2024/1689) Arts. 51-55, applicable from 2025-08-02; GPAI Code of Practice published 2025-07-10. Epoch (Apr 2025) put Bloc C at ~50k H100e vs Bloc B 110k.

items.summary: Bloc B's state council 'AI+' action guideline called for promoting an open-source ecosystem, consistent with its leading developers releasing frontier open weights throughout 2025. No 2025 gazette introduced licensing of weight release.
items.detail: Bloc B State Council, Opinions on deepening the 'AI+' action (Aug 2025; date from recollection). The 2023 Interim Measures for Generative AI Services require filing for public-facing services, not weight publication. Not verified via web_extract this run.
